The named router query projection already runs under autocast(enabled=False) in axis_collaboration.py:109. Its input depends on AMP expert computations, but attributing this directly to FP16 execution of the named linear layer would be incorrect.

The zero-weight implementation still runs the new backbone hook, selected-source projection and two unused graph losses. Their allocations, retained autograd objects and extra execution distinguish it from the parent. The current artifact does not identify which operation first changes a forward value, gradient or optimizer update.

SharedReadout.forward only applies the existing projection and adds its query parameter. Its underlying projection has LayerNorm/Linear/GELU/LayerNorm, not BatchNorm or Dropout. A hidden BN update or additional RNG consumption from that reference head is not supported by source.

The failure precedes saved graph gradient/loss comparisons. Near-zero effective gradient plus Adam amplification is plausible, especially for this small conditioning projection, but cannot be claimed without the named gradient, initial parameter, weight decay, epsilon and update evidence.
